text:
jordan: customer reports SSE stream missing final JSON object after they reconnect (auth refresh). payload ends mid-object, no finish_reason. repro attached from their client.

maya-platform: can you drop the request_id and model/region? also whether they use HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2, and which proxy (cloudflare/fastly) sits in front.

jordan: request_id: req_0b9c2a3a, model: redwood-1-large, region: us-west-2. They say HTTP/1.1 via a custom proxy (nginx) + an auth sidecar that rotates JWT and reconnects on 401. Happens ~30% of reconnects.

vikram-eng-sre: thanks. common pattern: client reconnects while server is mid-flush and proxy/nginx squeezes last chunk. finish_reason missing suggests server didn't emit final event. do we have backend logs for req_0b9c2a3a around 2026-03-12T18:12:03Z?

jordan: pasted from customer: 

```
data: {"id":"token_1","role":"assistant","content":"partial...\n"
data: {"id":"token_2","role":"assistant","content":"still streaming.."}
[connection closed]
```

Note: final JSON never arrived, they see truncated trailing bytes and parse errors on their JSON streaming parser.

ingrid-qa: can we get the server-side emitter trace? otherwise we should try to reproduce with a local nginx + token-rotate script. I can put together a small harness.

vikram-eng-sre: suggested repro steps for eng:
1) run a simple Node fetch stream to /v1/stream with long generation (2000 tokens)
2) put nginx as reverse proxy with proxy_buffering on and keepalive_timeout low
3) run an auth-renew agent that closes the client socket after the proxy retries (simulate sidecar refresh)
4) observe whether the final chunk ("finish_reason") is omitted or the connection terminates while JSON is partial.

maya-platform: also check for these server signals: aborted write syscalls, SIGPIPE, or write timeouts. If the runtime canceled the request due to connection reset then the final event may not be sent. We should correlate internal trace id -> logs for graceful shutdown path.

jordan: customer says they saw finish_reason:null in one case, and in others there's simply no closing brace. Parser error shows trailing bytes length 14. They use a parser that errors on invalid JSON.

vikram-eng-sre: quick mitigation for customer: recommend adding a small keepalive/event heartbeat emitted by client every 15s OR have the proxy forward with chunked transfer and disable aggressive buffering. Also try setting `Connection: close` on reconnect to force fresh connection rather than reuse pool. That often prevents truncated tail when proxy reuses sockets during auth swap.

ingrid-qa: i'm spinning up a repro now. initial findings: with default nginx proxy_buffering=on and proxy_request_buffering=on, we reproduce truncated tail when backend closes while proxy still has buffered data. Turning proxy_buffering off reduces incidence.

maya-platform: good. can eng add a server-side guard to try to flush a final sentinel event before closing? maybe an attempt to send `data: {"finish_reason":"server_shutdown"}\n\n` if close triggered by auth swap. if not feasible, document a recommended proxy config for customers (nginx/fastly) to avoid mid-stream truncation.

vikram-eng-sre: action items:
- eng (vikram) will fetch backend trace for req_0b9c2a3a and confirm whether final event was emitted.
- qa (ingrid) to finish repro and test nginx buffer settings and auth-rotation timings.
- platform (maya) to draft support KB with recommended proxy/nginx/fastly settings and quick workarounds (disable buffering, small client heartbeats, set Connection: close on reconnect).
- support (jordan) will send recommended mitigations to customer and ask for tcpdump if they want deep dive.

deploy-bot: deploy started: stream-runtime/flush-guard patch to staging (rollout id: r-2026-03-13-01). If probe shows improvement we'll promote.

jordan: noted, customer asked if this is a bug in our SSE implementation vs proxy behavior. answer: likely interaction with proxy/buffer + abrupt client reconnect. we should be cautious: if runtime never got to emit final chunk due to internal cancel it's on us. will follow up after trace.

vikram-eng-sre: confirmed in logs: for req_0b9c2a3a the runtime did schedule final emit but the server-side socket write returned EPIPE at final flush; subsequent close happened before proxy forwarded the last chunk. so root cause: backend write failed because client (or proxy) closed connection mid-flush during auth rotation.

jordan: sharing that with customer. they're going to try the proxy buffer settings and client-heartbeat workaround. asking whether we support a resume protocol for SSE (we don't today).

maya-platform: file a follow-up issue to evaluate a resume/ack sentinel for long streams. UX + cost tradeoffs are non-trivial but customers with long-lived streaming will benefit.

ingrid-qa: note for KB: include curl and Node repro snippets, nginx snippets:
```
# nginx snippets to try
proxy_buffering off;
proxy_request_buffering off;
proxy_http_version 1.1;
proxy_set_header Connection ""; # allow chunked
```

and client-side suggestion:
```
// node-fetch example: close and reopen for each major auth rotation
const res = await fetch(url, {headers: {Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, Connection: 'close'}})
res.body.on('data', chunk => parseSSE(chunk))
```

jordan: closing loop with customer now. will reopen if they still see truncated final object after config changes. :thumbsup:
